title: Week in Orbit
summary: This week, the space industry is a mixed bag of progress and setbacks, with SpaceX continuing its Starship saga while ULA grapples with financial turbulence. Meanwhile, the Defense Department is increasingly eyeing AI for defense applications, and the budget for space resilience is getting a boost.

themes.title: SpaceX's Starship Saga
themes.body: SpaceX's 13th test flight of the Starship demonstrates its relentless pursuit of orbital capability, though the road to operational status remains bumpy. Each test brings them closer, but also raises questions about the sustainability of their rapid-fire testing approach.

themes.title: ULA's Financial Woes
themes.body: United Launch Alliance is feeling the pinch from the grounding of its Vulcan rocket, raising concerns about its financial health and future contracts. As competition heats up, ULA's ability to rebound will be closely watched by investors and partners alike.

themes.title: AI in Defense
themes.body: With LatConnect 60 unveiling new AI capabilities, the defense sector's interest in artificial intelligence continues to grow, particularly in the Indo-Pacific region. This trend suggests a shift towards tech-driven solutions in military operations, potentially reshaping future engagements.

themes.title: Budget Boost for Space Resilience
themes.body: The FY27 budget markup adds $1.4 billion to the space resilience line, signaling a strong commitment to safeguarding U.S. interests in orbit. This funding could lead to increased collaboration and innovation among defense contractors as they vie for a piece of the pie.
